mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces earnings expectations and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when RSAFS falls > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the industrial production index above 0.5% signals improving manufacturing output, which boosts earnings growth and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when INDPRO rises > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25 percentage points signals a tightening monetary cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points and a decline in nonfarm payrolls above 50,000 signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls > 50,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls > 50,000 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 1% combined with a monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) above 10,000 units signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces earnings expectations and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > 1% AND HOUST falls > 10,000 units in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when RSAFS falls > 1% AND HOUST falls > 10,000 units (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the industrial production index above 0.5% combined with a monthly increase in capacity utilization above 0.5 percentage points signals improving supply conditions, which boosts earnings growth and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises > 0.5% AND HOUST rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when INDPRO rises > 0.5% AND HOUST rises > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).
